# Genesis Apocryphon Column 20 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 20 | **Condition:** Well preserved

---

**20:1** And Sarai wept that night because of my words. We journeyed and came to Zoan,

**20:2** and Sarai said to me concerning all the land of Egypt: Say of me, He is my brother,

**20:3** that I may live because of you. And Sarai wept also that night.

**20:4** Then Harkenosh came [...] with Lot, and Lot said to him [...] concerning Abram's wife [...]

**20:5** and Harkenosh brought gifts of silver and gold and fine linen [...] to the king.

**20:6** How beautiful is the form of her face, and how fine the hair of her head!

**20:7** How lovely are her eyes, and how pleasing is her nose

**20:8** and all the radiance of her countenance! How beautiful are her breasts

**20:9** and how lovely all her luminous skin! Her arms, how beautiful,

**20:10** and her hands, how graceful! How lovely are the palms of her hands!

**20:11** How long and fine are her fingers! Her feet, how beautiful!

**20:12** Her thighs, how smooth! No virgin or bride who enters the bridal chamber

**20:13** is more beautiful than she. Above all women her beauty is exalted;

**20:14** her beauty surpasses them all. And with all this beauty

**20:15** there is great wisdom in her, and all that she has is beautiful.

**20:16** And when the king heard the words of Harkenosh and the words of his two companions

**20:17** — for the three of them spoke as with one mouth — the king desired her greatly.

**20:18** And he sent and had her brought to him, and he saw her and was astonished at all her beauty.

**20:19** And he took her to himself as a wife, and he sought to kill me.

**20:20** But Sarai said to the king: He is my brother. And I, Abram, was spared on her account.

**20:21** And I, Abram, wept greatly, I and Lot my nephew, with me that night

**20:22** when Sarai was taken from me by force.

**20:23** I prayed that night and entreated and asked for mercy,

**20:24** and my tears ran down my face, and I said:

**20:25** Blessed are You, O God Most High, Lord of all the ages,

**20:26** for You are Lord and Master of all. You rule over all the kings of the earth

**20:27** to execute judgment upon them all. Now I cry out to You, my Lord,

**20:28** against Pharaoh Zoan, king of Egypt, for my wife has been taken from me by force.

**20:29** Execute judgment upon him for me, and let me see Your mighty hand

**20:30** descend upon him and upon all his household.

**20:31** May he not be able to defile my wife this night.

**20:32** And they shall know, all of them, that You are the Lord of all the kings of the earth.

**20:33** And I wept and was silent.

**20:34** And that night God Most High sent a pestilential spirit against him,

---

*SOPHIA notes: The beauty hymn is the crown jewel of the Genesis Apocryphon. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's formal structure but incorporates two of PNEUMA's superior readings: "luminous skin" (20:9) better captures the Aramaic than LOGOS's "fairness" or EMET's "whiteness"; "graceful" (20:10) for hands is more apt than "perfect." "Astonished" (20:18) is a compromise between LOGOS's "marveled" and PNEUMA's "stunned." The anaphoric "How beautiful/lovely" structure is preserved as essential to the hymn's literary character.*
